claim: A public employee establishes a prima facie case of First Amendment retaliation by demonstrating that protected speech was a substantial motivating factor in an adverse employment action, even where the employer articulates a legitimate non-retaliatory justification. The burden then shifts to the government to prove by a preponderance that the same decision would have been made absent the protected activity.
citation: Bascom v. Hargrove County Board of Supervisors, 738 F.3d 214 (4th Cir. 2019)
initial_reasoning: The citation to Bascom v. Hargrove County Board of Supervisors supports the claim as it aligns with the legal standard for First Amendment retaliation claims, which requires a plaintiff to show that protected speech was a substantial motivating factor in an adverse employment action, and then shifts the burden to the defendant to prove that the same decision would have been made regardless of the protected activity, as established by the Mount Healthy City School District Board of Education v. Doyle, 429 U.S. 274 (1977) and subsequent cases. The Bascom case is a relevant application of this standard in the 4th Circuit. The claim accurately reflects the legal framework for such cases.
